SnowDistribution: Winds approx 40-50 mph, making progress difficult. Hard going in the deeper drifts above 700 metres.  Blizzard and whiteout conditions presenting challenging and serious conditions.
Comment: Deteriorating weather is forecast later on Thursday as the next frontal system brings snow and strong winds.
WeatherInfluences: Strong South-South-Easterly winds will gradually increase in strength, becoming Gale force by the end of the period. Mostly dry with only a few light snow showers possible during the evening and into the morning. A complex freezing level with much terrain remaining frozen above 700 metres.
SnowStability: Recent deposits of fresh unstable windslab are present on North-West and North aspects above 950 metres. West and North-East aspects will also  be affected due to cross-loading. The greatest instability will be in steep locations such as gullies, gully tops, coire rims and convexities. On these aspects, cornices will be fragile. The avalanche hazard will be Considerable.
ObservedWeatherInfluences: Gale force South-South-East winds. Heavy snow overnight and into the morning eased to become mostly dry during the afternoon. Snow initially falling to lower elevations, then became confined to above 700 metres. The freezing level was around 950 metres.
ObservedSnowStability: Unstable windslab is lying on West through North to North-East to aspects above 1000 metres. The greatest instabilities are in steep locations such as gullies, gully tops, coire rims and convexities. Cornices are fragile and natural avalanche activity was observed on a North-West aspect at around 1050 metres. The avalanche hazard is Considerable.
